title: The Rising Brine of Saltpan Flat
story: Obrennoth the Brine Bellows squats in the middle of Saltpan Flat, pumping salty water into the low pans at 18 inches per hour. Three harvesters are stranded on a drying rack, and the brine is already 6 inches deep — the rack floods at 33 inches. Mr 6 cranks open the old sluice gate, which drains 13.5 inches per hour, and does the math before he starts running.
question: With brine rising 18 inches per hour and the sluice draining 13.5 inches per hour, how many hours does Mr 6 have before the brine climbs from 6 inches to the 33-inch flood line?
solution: The brine really rises by 18 - 13.5 = 4.5 inches each hour.
It must climb 33 - 6 = 27 inches to reach the rack.
praise: Subtracting the drain from the rise was the key insight — the step still needed was dividing the 27 inches left to climb by that net rate.
hint: Find the net rise per hour first, then see how many inches still have to be climbed.
victory: Mr 6 walked the harvesters out with twenty minutes to spare, and Obrennoth pumped itself hoarse against a sluice gate that simply out-subtracted it. It now bellows harmlessly into a pan marked FOR PICKLES ONLY.
imagePrompt: A bellows-shaped brine monster wheezing salty water across wide pale salt pans at dusk while a tiny numeral-6 knight hauls open a rusted sluice gate and three harvesters wave from a wooden drying rack.
